title: Inside the Pool of Gibeon: 3D Model Reconstruction and Some Observations About Finds
author: Maria Tamburrini
publisher: self-archived preprint (OSF/Academia.edu), Università degli Studi "La Sapienza" di Roma
allowedUseNotes: Copyrighted preprint/article. Project stores its own summary of the reported dating and stratigraphy only; no reproduction of the 3D model, plans, or photographs.
summary: A 3D digital reconstruction of Pritchard's excavated rock-cut pool at Tell el-Jib (Gibeon), paired with a reassessment of the finds recovered from its fill. Tamburrini reports the pool's original cutting/construction as datable to the 10th century BCE (Iron I/early Iron IIA), consistent with Pritchard's own excavation-era estimate that the pool was first dug near the start of the Iron Age. Separately, she describes a stratigraphically complex filling history: a substantial group of artifacts recovered from within the pool shaft dates to the 8th-6th centuries BCE, reflecting the pool's later reuse/disuse and infill over centuries, not its original excavation. This project's key finding from this source: the later Iron II material found in and around the pool documents the site's long subsequent occupation and the pool's eventual filling, not a later Iron II date for the pool's original construction — the construction itself sits at or before the early Iron IIA window 2 Samuel 2 requires.
confidenceNotes: Bibliographic details and the construction-vs-fill dating distinction are drawn from secondary web citations of this preprint (search-indexed summaries; DOI 10.31235/osf.io/5ajpc reported in secondary listings), not from direct inspection of the full paper. TO VERIFY: direct confirmation of the 10th-century construction date and the 8th-6th century fill dating against the paper's own stratigraphic argument and its citation of Pritchard's original excavation data.
